generators.carrier: finite-dim real vector spaces V, A with linear d: A -> V (declared)
J: V -> R, declared seminorm or cost
inf over alpha in A of J(delta - d alpha); depends only on coset [delta] when J is a seminorm

relations.statement: For J a seminorm, Phi_J(delta + d beta) = Phi_J(delta) for all beta in A
relations.hypotheses: J seminorm on V, d linear, A finite-dimensional
J: V -> R, d linear so d0 = 0

lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem L_upper {V A : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup A] (d : A →+ V) (J : V → ℝ) (δ : V) (hb : ∀ a, 0 ≤ J (δ - d a)) : sInf (Set.range fun a => J (δ - d a)) ≤ J δ := by sorry

lemmas.statement: For seminorm J, the infimum is constant on cosets modulo im d, so Phi_J is well defined on V/im d
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem L_invariance {V A : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup A] (d : A →+ V) (J : V → ℝ) (δ : V) (β : A) : sInf (Set.range fun a => J (δ + d β - d a)) = sInf (Set.range fun a => J (δ - d a)) := by sorry

near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Only the inequality Phi_J <= J holds; equality needs a shown infimum, e.g. when delta is orthogonal to im d in a suitable sense

near_misses.claim: Phi_J is coset-invariant for an arbitrary cost J
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Coset invariance needs J to be a seminorm, since a general cost gives a different infimum for each representative
